title: One CI run per merge: the merge tool rebuilds the records page before the ready run
why: shiv, Oct 31 14:12 CDT owner ask (via coordinator [ended:Claude-settings-coordinator-handoff]): second in work order. Owner figure: 25 of 80 merges in the week to Oct 31 needed a second CI run (not measured by triage). One second run measured at about 28 min (#882, Oct 30 20:10 CDT). FOURTH REPEAT 03:54 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 03:53, from runner 10's read of log merge3349b.log; unchecked by triage): `merge 3349 --confirm` refused a fully green ready PR because its generated records page went stale after main moved (#3279 landed); remedy is draft, records step, mark ready again, a second full CI (about 70 min, n=2; other repos unmeasured). The owner asked twice to stop the double CI run (Oct 31 14:12 CDT; Nov 1 20:51 CST, per decision records-index-at-merge, read by triage on origin/main). Triage read of how often the page goes stale (git log of docs/records.md on origin/main 4db2a9cf3, shallow clone, container time): since Nov 13 00:00, 227 commits on main and exactly 1 touched docs/records.md or docs/decisions or docs/debts: 15e889991, #3279 at 02:09 CST Nov 14; since Nov 10, 1 of 1409. So the page goes stale only when a merged PR changes records, not on every main move; #3349 met it because #3279 added a debt record (docs/debts/windows-shards-outgrow-caps.md). Stale-decision form (decision records-index-at-merge, sentence "That batch still runs CI twice (unmeasured in other repos; none in this repo, Oct 24 to 31)"): the "none in this repo" claim no longer holds: 70 min, n=2 here. Outcome the decision protects: main's records page current; what protects it now: the main-side check (lint/hook_catalog.py --check), and PR CI already waives a stale page (the coordinator's read). Fix to propose, in the order of least change: (a) the merge tool rebuilds the page in the merge commit, or (b) a main-side refresh PR after a records change, so a ready PR is never restarted; (c) the merge tool refuses stale and the remedy stays (today). Whether (a) breaks the tested-tree claim of push-skip-proven-tree (main's tree differs from the PR's tested tree by the page) is the lane's first read.
note: Placed ahead of c52 and every other open step but trust-card-guard: owner ask, Oct 31 14:12 CDT. Lane open, draft #895; it waits on batch 37, which also edits merge/merge.py. Cause: merge/merge.py (commit_claim) adds a 'Claim record numbers' commit and a 'Rebuild the records page' commit after the PR's ready run, and the push starts CI again. Fix: claim the numbers and rebuild docs/records.md before the PR goes ready, so the ready run is the only run. Guard rule records-page still keeps lanes from committing docs/records.md; the merge tool does it. Done check: merge/test_merge.py cases show no push after the ready run on a PR that changes a record summary, red on main and green on the fix. Needs no answer. Files: merge/merge.py, merge/test_merge.py. Done: #895 in batch 39 #916, main d657e1da (coordinator, Oct 31 20:01 CDT). Repeat, Nov 1 20:48 CST: the merge tool still rebuilt and pushed on a ready PR (batch 60, PR #1009), restarting CI. Follow-up: step records-stale-refuses-on-ready. Reopened 06:30 CST Nov 10, third repeat: batch 71c (#2510) went green at 9c13cfd98 after about 3.5 h of macOS jobs. The merge then refused a stale records page, and runner 8 pushed the page as 85ccaf60d. That push restarted the whole run (coordinator 06:29 CST Nov 10). The refusal on a ready PR is on main (merge/merge.py line 16, origin/main 0e6509a96), so step records-stale-refuses-on-ready may be landed; check it. Gap left: nothing stops a PR going ready before the draft records step ran on its head. Fix: the ready route (pr-ready-mcp-cloud) or the merge tool's draft step refuses ready, or marks the head, until the rebuilt page equals the tree. Decision records-index-at-merge.
